clues.text: Facing the square before the Water Gate, this scribe read the Book of the Law aloud from daybreak until noon.
In Jerusalem, a high wooden platform was built so this scribe could stand above the people while the Law was opened.
A scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, he came up from Babylon to Jerusalem during the reign of a Persian king.
King Artaxerxes wrote him a letter letting any willing Israelites, priests and Levites go with him to Jerusalem.
This priest set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, to practice it, and to teach it in Israel.
Weeping facedown before the house of God, he confessed Israel's sin as a large crowd gathered and wept with him.
Standing before the returned exiles, this priest told them they had been unfaithful by marrying foreign women.
